cell_type_model: CHO/HEK receptor-expression systems with human PROKR2; primary endometrial and immune-cell comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: PROK1 stimulation with radioligand binding, intracellular Ca2+ and second-messenger assays; G-protein and beta-arrestin interaction/ERK assays
relation_type: PROK1 binds and activates PROKR2, a prokineticin GPCR, with Gq/11-, Gi/o-, and arrestin-linked signaling
pathway_branch: PROK1-PROKR2 -> Gq/11-PLC-IP3-Ca2+ and Gi/o-ERK/beta-arrestin branches -> context-dependent cellular responses
limitations: Receptor coupling varies with expression system, ligand isoform, species, and cell context; the primary exact-pair work does not establish a unique terminal TF.

cell_type_model: CHO/HEK cells expressing PROKR1 and receptor-panel comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: PROK2 binding and stimulation; Ca2+, cAMP, G-protein, beta-arrestin, and ERK phosphorylation assays
relation_type: PROK2 binds and activates PROKR1 with concentration-dependent GPCR signaling
pathway_branch: PROK2-PROKR1 -> Gq/11-PLC-Ca2+ with Gi/o-ERK and context-dependent cAMP/arrestin signaling
limitations: PROK2 is generally more potent than PROK1 and coupling is assay dependent; no exact-pair terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: CHO/HEK PROKR2 expression systems; mouse SVZ-rostral migratory stream-olfactory bulb interneuron models
assay_or_perturbation: PROK2 binding and Ca2+/ERK assays; Prok2 or Prokr2 mutant mice with neuroblast migration and olfactory-bulb phenotyping
relation_type: PROK2 activates PROKR2 and the receptor pathway is required for olfactory interneuron migration
pathway_branch: PROK2-PROKR2 -> G-protein/Ca2+-ERK signaling -> SVZ-rostral migratory stream and olfactory-bulb interneuron migration
limitations: The migration phenotype is genetic/pathway-level and does not identify a unique terminal TF; recombinant receptor coupling remains context dependent.

cell_type_model: Human mesenchymal glioblastoma stem-cell spheres and mouse GBM tumors; purified/reporter TAM and mouse MEF receptor systems
assay_or_perturbation: PROS1 stimulation with AXL/TAM phosphorylation, reporter activation, ligand-trap and kinase-inhibitor assays; GBM conditioned-medium, NF-kappaB/p65, and growth assays
relation_type: PROS1-AXL activation is context-conflicted: GBM stem-cell models report PROS1-dependent AXL phosphorylation, whereas purified-receptor/MEF profiling finds PROS1 inactive as an AXL agonist
pathway_branch: PROS1-AXL -> AXL phosphorylation -> NF-kappaB/p65 and mesenchymal GBM growth in one tumor context; canonical TAM comparison excludes AXL activation
limitations: The positive result is restricted to a GBM tumor/microenvironment model and conflicts with receptor-isolated activation profiling; phosphatidylserine, ligand preparation, receptor abundance, and co-receptors may explain the discrepancy. No universal PROS1-AXL relay is established.

cell_type_model: Mertk-expressing mouse MEFs and primary retinal/phagocyte models; human and mouse macrophage comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: PROS1 stimulation with MERTK tyrosine-phosphorylation, receptor-isolation, apoptotic-cell phagocytosis, Mertk inhibition, and cytokine perturbation assays
relation_type: PROS1 binds and activates MERTK, especially in phosphatidylserine-dependent efferocytic contexts
pathway_branch: PROS1-MERTK plus PtdSer -> MERTK autophosphorylation -> efferocytosis and macrophage inflammatory-resolution outputs
limitations: Optimal activation depends on gamma-carboxylated PROS1, calcium, and PtdSer-bearing targets; downstream cytokine effects are cell-context dependent and no terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: Human SCC-25 head-and-neck and MGH-U3 bladder cancer cells; mouse Tyro3-expressing MEFs and neuronal comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: PROS1 stimulation with Tyro3 phosphorylation, ERK/AKT immunoblotting, soluble-receptor/antibody blockade, vitamin-K dependence, and survival assays
relation_type: PROS1 binds and activates TYRO3 and supports ligand-dependent ERK/AKT signaling
pathway_branch: PROS1-TYRO3 -> receptor autophosphorylation -> ERK and context-dependent AKT -> cancer-cell survival/proliferation or neuronal protection
limitations: PROS1 activity requires appropriate gamma-carboxylation and receptor/cell context; the cancer-cell ERK axis does not establish a universal terminal TF.

cell_type_model: HEK293T/COS-7 cells expressing GPR37; primary mouse cortical astrocytes and neuronal models
assay_or_perturbation: Prosaposin or prosaptide binding/pull-down, receptor internalization, GTP-gamma-S, cAMP, phospho-ERK, GPR37 knockdown, and oxidative-stress protection assays
relation_type: Prosaposin/prosaptide binds and activates GPR37 through a pertussis-toxin-sensitive G-protein relay
pathway_branch: PSAP-GPR37 -> Gi/o-cAMP inhibition and ERK phosphorylation -> astrocyte/neuronal stress protection
limitations: Prosaptide is an active prosaposin-derived fragment and several assays use receptor overexpression; trafficking and neuroprotection require receptor-associated cellular context. No terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: HEK293T/COS-7 cells expressing GPR37L1; primary mouse cortical astrocytes; later HEK293/U87 and cerebellar-slice comparator systems
assay_or_perturbation: Prosaposin/prosaptide binding, internalization, GTP-gamma-S, cAMP, and ERK assays with GPR37L1 expression or knockdown; later receptor-processing and ligand-rechallenge experiments
relation_type: Prosaposin/prosaptide was reported to activate GPR37L1, but later processing studies did not reproduce prosaptide activation, leaving the exact ligand-relay assignment unresolved
pathway_branch: PSAP-GPR37L1 -> reported Gi/o-cAMP inhibition and ERK phosphorylation -> astrocyte protection; competing evidence supports constitutive/processed-receptor regulation instead
limitations: The positive and negative results use different receptor processing, expression, and assay conditions; no consensus physiological PSAP-GPR37L1 relay or terminal TF endpoint is established.

cell_type_model: Cultured mammalian cells, mouse efferent-duct epithelium, and lysosomal sorting models
assay_or_perturbation: Prosaposin C-terminal truncation/co-immunoprecipitation, sortilin loss-of-function, trafficking, endocytosis, and lysosomal localization assays
relation_type: PSAP binds SORT1/sortilin for biosynthetic and endocytic lysosomal sorting rather than canonical intracellular receptor signaling
pathway_branch: PSAP-SORT1 -> TGN/endocytic sorting -> lysosomal delivery and processing of prosaposin/saposins
limitations: Sortilin is a Vps10-family trafficking receptor in this context; the evidence does not support a direct kinase, adaptor, or TF relay through SORT1.

cell_type_model: Rat osteoblast/osteoblast-like cultures and primary mouse osteogenic-lineage cells; conditional Cdh2 mouse bone models
assay_or_perturbation: PTH stimulation with PTH1R-LRP6 co-immunoprecipitation, phospho-LRP6, Axin recruitment, beta-catenin stabilization, PKA inhibition, LRP6 knockdown, and bone-formation assays
relation_type: PTH activation of PTH1R recruits LRP6 into a ternary receptor complex and phosphorylates LRP6; this is a receptor-complex relay, not direct PTH-LRP6 binding
pathway_branch: PTH-PTH1R -> PKA -> PTH1R/LRP6-Axin -> beta-catenin/TCF-LEF transcriptional activity -> osteoblast activity and bone formation
limitations: The exact Module20A edge is PTH-LRP6, but PTH binds PTH1R and LRP6 is a recruited Wnt coreceptor; no direct PTH-LRP6 ligand-binding assay was found. Beta-catenin is retained as a provisional downstream endpoint.

cell_type_model: COS-7/HEK293 receptor-expression systems and osteoblast/osteogenic comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: PTH binding and cAMP assays; PTH1R trafficking, beta-arrestin/dynamin perturbation, Gq/ERK and EGFR-transactivation assays
relation_type: PTH binds and activates the class-B GPCR PTH1R through Gs/cAMP and Gq/PLC-linked signaling
pathway_branch: PTH-PTH1R -> Gs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP/PKA and Gq-PLC-Ca2+ -> receptor trafficking, EGFR-transactivation, and ERK outputs
limitations: PTH1R signaling is ligand-conformation, receptor-trafficking, and cell-context dependent; the cited exact-pair studies do not establish a unique terminal TF.

cell_type_model: HEK293 and COS-7 cells stably or transiently expressing human/rat PTH2R
assay_or_perturbation: PTH(1-34) binding, receptor mutagenesis, cAMP accumulation, and intracellular-Ca2+ assays
relation_type: PTH activates PTH2R with strong human-receptor and weaker species-dependent activity
pathway_branch: PTH-PTH2R -> Gs-adenylyl cyclase-cAMP with weaker cell-context-dependent Ca2+ signaling
limitations: PTH2R is preferentially activated by TIP39 and PTH potency varies across human, rat, and zebrafish receptors; no exact-pair cellular function or terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells stably expressing human PTH1R/PTH2R and receptor-selectivity assay systems
assay_or_perturbation: TIP39 binding, cAMP competition, receptor selectivity, and antagonist assays
relation_type: TIP39/PTH2 binds PTH1R with moderate or low affinity but does not activate it and can antagonize PTH/PTHrP signaling
pathway_branch: TIP39-PTH1R -> receptor occupancy/antagonism without a productive PTH1R relay
limitations: The result is ligand binding and antagonism, not activation; affinity and antagonist potency vary with TIP39 truncation and receptor species. No terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: HEK293 PTH2R-expression systems, primary rat dorsal-root-ganglion neurons, and mouse CFK2 chondrocytes with PTH2R
assay_or_perturbation: TIP39 binding and cAMP/Ca2+ assays; PTH2R transfection, pharmacologic stimulation, and chondrocyte proliferation/differentiation/Sox9 reporter assays
relation_type: TIP39/PTH2 binds and activates PTH2R and produces receptor-proximal cAMP/Ca2+ signaling with cellular differentiation outputs
pathway_branch: PTH2-TIP39-PTH2R -> Gs-cAMP and Gq/Ca2+ -> nociceptive or chondrocyte differentiation outputs with reduced SOX9 transcription
limitations: TIP39 is the endogenous PTH2R ligand; chondrocyte and neuronal outputs are model-specific and do not imply a universal terminal program.

cell_type_model: Primary rat hippocampal neurons, COS-7 PTH1R membrane systems, and human H1944 lung-adenocarcinoma cells
assay_or_perturbation: PTHrP(1-34/1-36) binding and cAMP/Ca2+ assays; PTH1R knockdown, cAMP analogs, ERK perturbation, and proliferation assays
relation_type: PTHrP/PTHLH binds and activates PTH1R through cAMP/Ca2+ and context-dependent ERK signaling
pathway_branch: PTHLH-PTH1R -> Gs-cAMP/PKA and Ca2+ with ERK cross-talk -> neuronal, epithelial, or osteogenic cellular outputs
limitations: PTHrP isoform and cell context determine sustained versus transient signaling; the cited studies do not establish a unique terminal TF for this exact pair.

cell_type_model: HEK293/COS-7 cells expressing human or rat PTH2R and PTH/PTHrP receptor chimeras
assay_or_perturbation: PTHrP binding/selectivity, cAMP response, receptor chimeras, and engineered PTHrP hybrid-peptide assays
relation_type: PTHrP has negligible native PTH2R activation and is strongly disfavored relative to PTH/TIP39; engineered residue substitutions can create artificial PTH2R agonists
pathway_branch: PTHLH-PTH2R -> absent or negligible native cAMP relay; engineered hybrid controls define the receptor-selectivity boundary
limitations: This is an explicit negative/selectivity boundary, not evidence for a downstream PTHLH-PTH2R pathway; engineered analogues must not be transferred to native PTHrP. No terminal TF endpoint was measured.

cell_type_model: ALK-expressing mammalian cell lines, glioblastoma cultures, and mouse hematopoietic stem/progenitor-cell models
assay_or_perturbation: PTN binding to ALK ECD, radioligand/cell binding, ALK phosphorylation, IRS-1/Shc/PLC-gamma/PI3K assays, ALK perturbation, RAS-MEK-ERK, and growth assays
relation_type: PTN directly binds ALK and activates its receptor-tyrosine-kinase signaling complex
pathway_branch: PTN-ALK -> ALK autophosphorylation -> IRS1/Shc/PLC-gamma/PI3K and RAS-MEK-ERK -> growth, neurite, or hematopoietic outputs
limitations: PTN processing state and receptor/co-receptor composition alter the response; some hematopoietic effects require PTPRZ1-dependent ALK activation. No unique terminal TF was assigned to the exact PTN-ALK edge.

cell_type_model: Human endothelial cells and U87MG/glioma cells expressing alpha-v-beta-3 integrin and PTPRZ1
assay_or_perturbation: PTN binding/capture and blocking antibodies or beta3 specificity-loop peptide; beta3 Y773 phosphorylation, Src inhibition, integrin/PTPRZ1 interaction, and migration assays
relation_type: PTN directly interacts with integrin alpha-v-beta-3 and promotes a PTPRZ1-dependent integrin/Src relay
pathway_branch: PTN-alpha-v-beta-3/PTPRZ1 complex -> beta3 Y773 phosphorylation and c-Src -> endothelial or glioma-cell migration
limitations: Alpha-v-beta-3 is an adhesion-receptor complex and PTPRZ1 is required for the measured relay; the result does not establish a standalone PTN-integrin kinase pathway or terminal TF.

cell_type_model: Mouse oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, human/mouse glioblastoma stem-cell models, and mouse hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells
assay_or_perturbation: PTN stimulation or blockade; PTPRZ1 binding/phosphatase assays, PTPRZ1 knockdown, phospho-ALK/Src/ERK, RAS/MEK inhibition, differentiation, tumor-growth, and HSPC-expansion assays
relation_type: PTN binding inhibits PTPRZ1 phosphatase activity and organizes PTPRZ1-dependent kinase and cellular-function branches
pathway_branch: PTN-PTPRZ1 -> PTP inhibition/Src-ALK-GRB2-RAS-MEK-ERK -> oligodendrocyte differentiation, glioma-stem-cell maintenance, or HSPC output
limitations: PTPRZ1 isoform and chondroitin-sulfate state are important; ERF phosphorylation was measured in a hematopoietic model only and is not a universal endpoint.

cell_type_model: COS-1 cells expressing human NPY1R and rat IEC-6 intestinal epithelial cells expressing human Y1R
assay_or_perturbation: PYY binding, Ca2+/forskolin-cAMP assays, pertussis-toxin and Gbeta-gamma perturbation, Src/EGFR/PKC inhibitors, ERK phosphorylation, and epithelial-growth assays
relation_type: PYY activates NPY1R/Y1R through Gi/o-linked signaling with EGFR transactivation and MAPK output
pathway_branch: PYY-NPY1R -> Gi/o-Gbeta-gamma-Src/EGFR-PKC -> ERK/MAPK -> intestinal epithelial proliferation
limitations: The strongest functional mechanism uses an engineered IEC-6 model and receptor expression; endogenous PYY processing and tissue context may change the branch. No terminal TF was measured.

cell_type_model: HEK293 cells expressing human NPY2R/Y2R and receptor-pharmacology systems using radiolabeled PYY
assay_or_perturbation: PYY binding, receptor expression cloning, forskolin-stimulated cAMP inhibition, and intracellular-Ca2+ assays
relation_type: PYY binds and activates NPY2R/Y2R with Gi/o-linked inhibition of cAMP and cell-context-dependent Ca2+ signaling
pathway_branch: PYY-NPY2R -> Gi/o-adenylyl-cyclase inhibition and context-dependent Ca2+ signaling
limitations: PYY1-36 and PYY3-36 differ in potency and processing; the exact-pair evidence is strongest in heterologous systems and no terminal TF or pair-specific cellular output was measured.

cell_type_model: COS-7/HEK293T cells expressing human NPY5R with engineered G-protein/calcium-flux assay systems
assay_or_perturbation: PYY binding-site mapping, photo-crosslinking, alanine scanning, double-cycle mutagenesis, and PYY-evoked receptor activation/calcium-flux assays
relation_type: PYY binds and activates NPY5R/Y5R, with receptor-proximal signaling captured in a chimeric G-protein calcium assay
pathway_branch: PYY-NPY5R -> Y5R GPCR activation -> G-protein-linked Ca2+ flux; no native-cell downstream function was resolved
limitations: The primary activation assay uses a chimeric G-protein system and the paper focuses on receptor-interface mapping; physiological coupling and terminal TF output remain unresolved.

cell_type_model: CHO cells expressing human QRFPR/GPR103 and rodent hypothalamic or pituitary comparator models
assay_or_perturbation: QRFP/26RFa binding and dose-response assays, G-alpha-16 calcium flux, receptor mutagenesis/glycosylation, and central peptide administration
relation_type: QRFP/26RFa binds and activates QRFPR/GPR103, a RFamide GPCR
pathway_branch: QRFP-QRFPR -> Gq/Gi-linked Ca2+ and cAMP signaling -> energy-homeostasis, feeding, and neuroendocrine outputs
limitations: QRFP peptide length and receptor glycosylation affect potency; in vivo feeding phenotypes do not by themselves identify a terminal TF or a single native G-protein branch.

cell_type_model: Human CMKLR1-transfected cells, human primary skeletal-muscle cells, and monocyte/dendritic-cell chemotaxis models
assay_or_perturbation: Chemerin binding, BRET G-protein/arrestin biosensors, Ca2+ mobilization, ERK phosphorylation, receptor internalization, chemotaxis, and CMKLR1/ERK perturbation
relation_type: Chemerin/RARRES2 activates CMKLR1/ChemR23 through Gi/o and beta-arrestin-linked signaling
pathway_branch: RARRES2-CMKLR1 -> Gi/o and beta-arrestin2 -> Ca2+/ERK1/2 -> chemotaxis or metabolic-cell output
limitations: Chemerin processing state, receptor expression, and cell type strongly affect signaling; GPR1 and CCRL2 can bind chemerin but are not interchangeable with CMKLR1. No terminal TF was assigned.

cell_type_model: HepG2 cells, NIH3T3-L1 adipocytes, mouse white adipose tissue/skeletal muscle, and STRA6-positive cancer models
assay_or_perturbation: Holo-RBP4/retinol stimulation with STRA6/JAK2/STAT phosphorylation, CRBP1/LRAT perturbation, STRA6 knockdown or mutants, STAT reporters, SOCS3 expression, and metabolic/transformation assays
relation_type: Holo-RBP4 binds STRA6 as a retinol transporter-signaling receptor and activates a JAK2/STAT3/STAT5 cascade
pathway_branch: RBP4-STRA6 plus CRBP1/LRAT -> STRA6/JAK2 -> STAT3/STAT5 -> SOCS3, insulin-resistance, or oncogenic cellular outputs
limitations: Signaling requires holo-RBP4/retinol and is interdependent with CRBP1 and LRAT; STAT3 versus STAT5 usage is cell-specific. This is a transporter-receptor relay, not a direct RBP4-TF interaction.
